Q: git clone only the given submodule(s) which are submodules of another submodule A:

This is a distinctly unusual workflow, but hey, with Git the answer to even halfway-sane "can I…?" questions is literally by definition "yes."

Basically, telling Git not to do things that make normal workflows fast and efficient takes work, so you're going to have to spend some time telling it "no, really no, do just this little part."

git fetch --filter=tree:1 --depth=1 --no-tags $(git config -f .gitmodules submodule.MainSubmodule.url) $maintag
git show FETCH_HEAD:.gitmodules >sub_gitmodules
git remote add subsub $(git config -f sub_gitmodules submodule.neededsubmodule.url)

and from there how you set up your super-selective subsubmodule slice is going to depend on details not present in your question.

Q: Reading a plain text file in Java A:

Java NIO.2

Use the Java NIO.2 features, such as Paths and Files utility classes.

Files.readString

Read entire file into memory as a String object.

String content = Files.readString(Paths.get("sample.txt"));  // Java 11+

Character encoding defaults to UTF-8. Every US-ASCII file is also a UTF-8 file.

Files.readAllLines

Or read the file as list of lines.

List<String> content = Files.readAllLines(Paths.get("sample.txt"));  // Java 8+

Also defaults to UTF-8.

Files.readAllBytes

Access the content as bytes.

byte[] bytes = new Files.readAllBytes(Paths.get("sample.txt"));

Q: Learning coding from scratch A:

As others have suggested, Python is a good starting language for people with no prior experience. The Python Tutorial is a good place to learn from.

Q: Sonar exclusions/inclusions A:

While you can exclude some files from coverage, you can only include files as a whole. That is, exclusion is granular, but inclusion is not (i.e. sonar.coverage.inclusions doesn't exist), so I don't think this will work the way you're currently trying to do it.

That said, this should be doable with only exclusions if you craft them carefully, i.e. **/model/*.java rather than **/model/**/*.java.

Q: Is there a NumPy function that allows you to specify start, step, and number? A:

The shortest and most elegant way (from my perspective) is:

import numpy as np

start = 0
step = 1.25
num = 9

result = start + np.arange(0, num) * step

returns

[  0.     1.25   2.5    3.75   5.     6.25   7.5    8.75  10.  ]
